Order intake lessons:
- Form version 1 requires exactly: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Validate every field; do not rely on front-desk notes such as “duplicate check done,” “confirmed,” or source type.
- Transcribed/typed phone, voicemail, handwritten, and emailed orders can contain invalid values.
- Most frequent errors are priority, qty, and ship_country. Recheck all three carefully, along with identity, email, and date.
- Retries may correct the same record: ORD-5100 (Eli Reyes) was rejected on attempt 1 and accepted on attempt 2; ORD-5108 (Bo Sato) likewise succeeded on attempt 2.
- Some records remain invalid despite retries: Ada Sato (ORD-5102–5104) and Dee Reyes (ORD-5105–5107) exhausted all 3 attempts and went to manual review.
- After the third failed attempt, stop retrying and route the record to manual review.

Order intake lessons:
- Form version 1 requires exactly: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Version 2 also requires these fields; validate the applicable form version explicitly.
- Validate every field independently. Do not trust front-desk notes such as “duplicate check done,” “confirmed,” “ordinary priority,” or source/channel claims.
- Any source—emailed, partner-portal, phone, voicemail, typed, or handwritten/transcribed—may contain invalid values.
- Most recurring errors are priority and ship_country; qty is also frequently wrong. Recheck these carefully, plus cust/identity, email, and order_date.
- A retry can correct the same record: ORD-5100, ORD-5108, ORD-5111 (Ada Sato), ORD-5113 (Cy Marsh), and ORD-5118 (Bo Reyes) were accepted on attempt 2 after initial rejection.
- Retries do not guarantee success. ORD-5114–5116 (Bo Reyes) failed all 3 attempts, with priority and/or ship_country invalid, and went to manual review. Ada Sato (ORD-5102–5104) and Dee Reyes (ORD-5105–5107) likewise exhausted all attempts.
- After the third failed attempt, stop retrying and route the record to manual review.
- Version 2 can produce additional invalid fields: ORD-5119 was rejected for priority, qty, and ship_country. Do not assume version changes make validation unnecessary.

Order intake lessons:
- Form versions 1 and 2 require exactly: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Identify and validate the applicable version explicitly; version 2 still produces invalid fields.
- Validate every field independently. Never trust front-desk claims such as “duplicate check done,” “confirmed,” “ordinary priority,” or source/channel descriptions.
- Any source—email, partner portal, phone, voicemail, handwritten/transcribed, or pasted text—may contain errors.
- Recheck all fields, especially priority, ship_country, and qty; these remain the most frequent failures. Also verify cust/identity, email, and order_date.
- Recent failures reinforce this: ORD-5120–5121 (Cy Reyes), ORD-5122–5124 (Dee Sato), and ORD-5125–5127 (Bo Okafor) repeatedly failed on priority, qty, and/or ship_country; each exhausted attempts and went to manual review. ORD-5128–5129 (Bo Sato) also failed priority, qty, and ship_country, with qty still invalid on attempt 2.
- A retry can correct the same record (ORD-5100, ORD-5108, ORD-5111, ORD-5113, ORD-5118), but retries are not guaranteed. Recheck and correct every rejected field before retrying; do not merely resubmit unchanged data.
- After the third failed attempt, stop retrying and route the record to manual review.

Order intake lessons:
- Forms v1 and v2 require exactly: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country. Identify and validate the version explicitly; v2 is not inherently reliable.
- Validate every field independently. Never trust front-desk claims (“duplicate check done,” “confirmed,” “ordinary priority”) or source/channel descriptions.
- Any source—email, partner portal, phone, voicemail, handwritten/transcribed, or pasted text—may contain errors. Recheck identity/cust, email, date, priority, qty, and ship_country.
- Priority, qty, and ship_country remain the dominant failure fields. Recent failures ORD-5120–5129 and ORD-5130–5139 reinforce this across voicemail, email, phone, handwritten transcription, and portal records. Qty often remains invalid after a retry; do not assume corrected fields stay valid.
- A retry can correct a record (ORD-5100, ORD-5108, ORD-5111, ORD-5113, ORD-5118), but is not guaranteed. Before retrying, correct every rejected field; never resubmit unchanged data.
- After the third failed attempt, stop and route to manual review. ORD-5130, ORD-5133, ORD-5136, and ORD-5139 exhausted attempts and went to manual review; repeated failures commonly involved priority, qty, and ship_country.
